source_basis.predecessor_source_reuse: Pure computational continuation of the role-local exact-curtailment, fresh-audit, rho=.20 and synchronous-batch wall model; no new external empirical claim introduced.

tested_model.terminal_rule: commit iff W_r>=k with exact deterministic curtailment
tested_model.batch_semantics: candidate stages serial; b paired observations launched synchronously within a stage; launched batch is paid in full; stage wall cost ceil(N_stage/b); false commit terminates stream

global_certificate_method.enumeration: Enumerated all 246729 length-20 action-count vectors satisfying exact all-null FWER<=.05; exchange-sort by increasing p1/(1-p0) gives each multiset's globally maximal worst-position q=.60 true-commit power.
global_certificate_method.exact_order_independent_wall_bound: For every multiset and each b in {4,8,16,32}, compute each action's exact null conditional-survival stage-round PMF from the curtailed discordant-sign stopping law mixed with the NegativeBinomial waiting law at rho=.20, convolve all 20 stage-round PMFs, and form the optimistic total CDF (1-S)+S*F_surv by assigning every false-commit path zero wall cost. Its q95 is an order-independent necessary lower bound on achievable exact wall q95.
global_certificate_method.exact_readout: For each optimistic power breakpoint, exact-read the all-null stopped wall-cost distribution under an exchange-maximin order. If the exact q95 missed the optimistic budget, enumerate every multiset attaining that optimistic power/budget and solve a finite count-state dynamic program over all orderings that preserve the target worst-position power. At fixed budget B, the reject contribution of a next action depends only on the prefix multiset because survival-PMF multiplication is commutative, so the DP exactly maximizes total CDF(B) without enumerating path distributions separately for every ordering.
global_certificate_method.numerics: float64 finite binomial/negative-binomial recursions and convolutions. Per-action round-PMF truncation maxima were 1200/600/300/200 rounds for b=4/8/16/32; residual tail at those maxima was at floating-zero scale (<=1.2e-16 in normalization checks), well beyond every certified q95 breakpoint.

interpretation: The predecessor's broad direct wall screen is now replaced, inside the tested finite action class, by a global exact wall-round certificate over every admissible multiset and every ordering capable of preserving each multiset's maximin power.
No hidden pair-count-suboptimal multiset exists outside the previous surrogate screen that improves the certified q95 wall frontier for b=4,8,16,32.

Ordering remains a real cost control variable: exact power-preserving reorderings close razor budgets at b4=413/750, b8=206 and b16=181. Conversely several optimistic multiset bounds are unattainable by any power-preserving ordering; the DP quantifies the CDF shortfall rather than guessing from exchange order.

At b32 one optimistic power level (0.053395984646347566 at B=115) disappears entirely because the next higher power 0.053465547907689266 is feasible at the same exact q95=116; this explains the 36-point exact frontier from 37 optimistic breakpoints.
rejected_or_narrowed_generalizations: Rejected within the tested finite model: the previous surrogate-based wall screen might have missed a materially better multiset. Full enumeration and razor ordering DP found none.
Rejected: exchange-maximin ordering is always wall-q95 optimal among power-preserving orders. Several razor budgets require a different order to attain the global wall frontier.

Narrowed: these frontiers are certificates only for 20 candidates, the 14 listed exact curtailed actions, q_good=.60, fresh independent audits, rho=.20 sign-clock cost baseline, synchronous fixed-size within-candidate batches and serial candidate generation. They do not certify variable latency, stragglers, asynchronous refill/cancel, cross-candidate concurrency, intermediate r values, stochastic deepening, multiple simultaneous good candidates, or reused adaptive audit data.
